name: Ashwagandha

lead: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) is a shrub whose root is a staple of Ayurvedic medicine. Extracts are marketed as adaptogens for stress, sleep and vitality.

In fitness use it is taken to support strength, recovery and testosterone. Small randomized trials report modest gains in strength and some hormone readings; the samples are small and funding is often industry-linked, and the wiki's rating is moderate.

paras: The active constituents are withanolides, which appear to modulate the stress axis, lower cortisol and affect GABAergic and inflammatory signalling. Researchers suggest any effect on muscle likely comes indirectly through improved stress, sleep and recovery rather than direct anabolism.

Ashwagandha is sold as a supplement in most countries. Rare cases of liver injury have been reported, and it can affect thyroid hormone levels and cause drowsiness or stomach upset. It is generally avoided in pregnancy and may interact with thyroid, sedative and immunosuppressant drugs.
